solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: For example, Lima to Landlord

blocks.note: Lima is an example of a capital city, that of Peru
a landlord is one who lets property

explanation.surface: Someone gives an example of a journey or a message going from Lima to a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the shared initial: the L that begins both Lima and Landlord is an upper-case character.
explanation.definitionFit: The initial L standing at the start of both proper nouns is a big upper-case character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Divine lilac trees from which rook’s taken off

indicators.note: 'from which ... taken' says a letter is removed from the words just named
something off is out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: Lilac trees look heavenly once a rook has flown off them.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from LILACTREES, leaving LILACTEES, then rearrange to CELESTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means heavenly or godlike, a close synonym of divine as an adjective.

clue.text: Average salmon aimed at vulgar types we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the pieces are spelt as words that sound the same

blocks.note: a parr is a young salmon
as in heading for, making for
coarse people are vulgar

explanation.surface: An ordinary fish is lobbed at some uncouth people.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes what is normal or expected, taken from golf where par is the standard score.

clue.text: In poetry, star-crossed lovers’ meeting

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of poetry runs into the start of star

explanation.surface: Romeo and Juliet, the star-crossed lovers of poetry, meet in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a private romantic appointment arranged between two people in love.

clue.text: Wife who barely got up to protest

definitions.text: Wife who barely got up to protest

blocks.clueFragment: Wife who barely got up to protest
blocks.note: surface reading: a married woman who hardly bothered to stand up and object
setter's reading: got up means dressed, so barely got up means dressed in nothing at all

explanation.surface: A lazy wife who could hardly rouse herself to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the wife of Earl Leofric rode naked through Coventry to protest against his taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblewoman of legend is a wife whose protest ride was made unclothed through the streets of Coventry.

clue.text: Drugs said to make you relax

indicators.note: said means spoken, so what is meant is a word sounding like the drugs

blocks.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so several are Es

explanation.surface: Someone recommends drugs as a way to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or slacken, a verb synonym for becoming or making less tense.

clue.text: Cryptic setter is concealing answer papers

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are scrambled
concealing means holding something hidden within

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A crossword setter hides the solutions to the exam papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Note 'is' does double duty in the surface but here is part of the letters to rearrange; 'concealing' alone takes the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatises are formal written studies of a subject, which can be called papers.

clue.text: Pub life, a chronic drunken state for some

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Life spent in the pub leaves a chronic drunk in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For some' is fair because the official name of Taiwan is recognised as a country only by some nations.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official title of Taiwan, a country whose statehood only a few governments formally recognise.

clue.text: Drive ultimately ending in river

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept
in tells us one piece is placed inside the next

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A car journey that finally finishes in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive in the sense of an inner impulse or compulsion is an urge.

clue.text: Service to erase computing bug

indicators.note: erasing wipes out letters, so a piece is taken away

blocks.note: a liturgy is a form of church service
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A tech support service sets out to wipe a software bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computing bug' looks like one phrase, but the bug here is an illness; the dreaded lurgy is British slang for any unspecified infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug in the sense of a minor infection or virus matches the jokey British slang word lurgy.

clue.text: Boxers may get sick of this underworld character

definitions.text: Boxers may get sick of this

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
temper as in temperament or nature

explanation.surface: Fighters tire of a villain from the criminal underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxers are dogs, not fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a viral disease of dogs, and boxers are a dog breed that can catch it.

clue.text: Need Scotch, say, to mature

blocks.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, such as whisky
to age is to mature, as whisky does

explanation.surface: Scotch whisky needs time to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or deficiency, which is what need means as a noun.

clue.text: Sound accommodation for animals

blocks.note: first meaning: secure, firm, steady
second meaning: a building where horses are kept

explanation.surface: Solid, well-built housing for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means firm and steady, while the noun names a building that houses horses.

clue.text: Craftsman’s pit working to bring in graduates

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside

blocks.note: a stone is the pit of a fruit
on as in operating, switched on
MA is a Master of Arts, so several are MAs

explanation.surface: A craftsman's quarry pit takes on university graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests a quarry, fitting the craftsman, but it is a fruit stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses stone, a type of craftsman.

clue.text: Pals protect one beginning to defy bullies

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
to protect something is to surround and shield it

blocks.note: intimates are close friends
I is the Roman numeral one
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Friends stand guard over a lone pupil who stands up to the bullies.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullies as a verb means frightens or coerces someone, which is what intimidates means.

clue.text: Evening Mass comes over as vilifying

indicators.note: in a down clue coming over means sitting above, so this piece goes first

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
evening as in making level or straight

explanation.surface: An evening church Mass turns into a session of slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like the time of day, but it is the verb to even, making things level.
explanation.definitionFit: Maligning means speaking ill of someone, a direct synonym of vilifying or slandering.

clue.text: Passion found in diaries now and again

indicators.note: now and again means at intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone's diaries reveal occasional fits of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger or rage, a strong emotion that passion can name.

clue.text: River crustacean larvae, extremely vile

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crab is a crustacean
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: River crustacean larvae are utterly disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means dreadful or abominable, so it is a strong synonym for vile.

clue.text: Shelter inside from freezing rain

indicators.note: inside means the interior, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: freezing rain is sleet, whose middle letters are kept

explanation.surface: Taking shelter indoors out of the sleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee is the sheltered side away from the wind, so it means shelter or cover.

clue.text: Job on set playing an explorer

indicators.note: playing means performing or fooling about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: a living is a job or means of earning
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor working on a film set plays the part of an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: David Livingstone was the Scottish missionary who explored central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian missionary famously travelled through Africa, so he counts as an explorer.

clue.text: Faint on vacation, giddy after drink

indicators.note: vacating means emptying, so the inside letters leave and only the ends stay
after says this piece follows the next one

blocks.note: grog is rum and water, or any alcoholic drink
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker feels faint and dizzy after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint as an adjective describes feeling weak and dazed, which is what groggy means.

clue.text: Clogs seen as superior heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: smug means self-satisfied, feeling superior

explanation.surface: Wooden clogs seen as upmarket footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clogs' looks like shoes, but it is a verb, as in gums up.
explanation.definitionFit: To gum something up is to clog it with sticky matter, so gums matches clogs as a verb.

clue.text: Burning wood abandoned by English tree hugger

indicators.note: being abandoned means being left behind, so a letter departs

blocks.note: an ember is a glowing piece of wood in a dying fire
E is the abbreviation for English
an acer is a maple tree

explanation.surface: An English environmentalist walks away from a forest fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree hugger' reads as one phrase, but tree supplies letters and hugger alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who embraces another person is literally a hugger, an agent noun from the verb.

clue.text: People’s careers

blocks.note: first meaning: peoples, ethnic groups
second meaning: rushes headlong

explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like jobs, but it is the verb meaning to hurtle; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names groups of humankind sharing descent, while the verb means hurtles along at speed.

clue.text: Meagre tip

blocks.note: first meaning: scant, thin
second meaning: tilt or slope

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a stingy gratuity, but tip is the verb to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes thin or scanty times, and the verb means incline to one side.

clue.text: Nice cheers, not so cruel

blocks.note: merci is French for thanks, as said in the city of Nice
less means not as much

explanation.surface: Pleasant cheering that turns out to be less cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective, but it is the French Riviera city, so the cheers are French.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciless means showing no pity or compassion, a close synonym of cruel.

clue.text: Scale from cayman’s front leg?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A scale taken off the front leg of a cayman, a kind of crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like the reptile's skin, but it is the verb to ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to ascend it, which is what climb means as a verb.

clue.text: Embarrassment results from misdirecting soldiers

blocks.note: surface reading: an officer is shamed after sending troops the wrong way
setter's reading: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, and a missed dip ends up on your cheek

explanation.surface: A commander is humiliated after sending his troops the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain soldiers are fingers of toast for dunking in a boiled egg; aim one badly and the yolk lands on your face.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means looking foolish or humiliated after a blunder, which is embarrassment.
